**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-14**
**Member:** Morgan Ellison
**Member ID:** W176862845
**Reference number:** POC-5FADD4BBDE-47544
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), State of Iowa
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0287 – Hip Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/200_299/0287.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Aetna denied on 2026-08-14 under reference number POC-5FADD4BBDE-47544. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that I need.

I am relying on the plan's own medical policy, Aetna CPB 0287 – Hip Arthroplasty. Below I quote the plan's criteria and match each one to what is already in my medical record.

---

### 1. Advanced joint disease with pain and functional disability

The plan's policy states:

> "Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs) from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the hip joint; and"

My records establish this. I have had 12 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I walk with a cane, I can only manage about one block, and I cannot put on my own shoes without help. Those are ordinary daily activities, and I can no longer do them.

### 2. Physical examination findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Limited range of motion (ROM), antalgic gait, and pain in hip joint with passive ROM on physical examination"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. My records also document that I ambulate with a cane and am limited to one block.

### 3. Radiographic evidence — the reason given for the denial

This is the criterion the denial notice points to. The plan's policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of either of the following: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) with stage II or III disease; or Moderate/severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint (Tonnis grade 2 or 3; see Appendix for Tonnis grading scale); and"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of 2026-05-31 reports joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. That is the study that was submitted, and those are the findings it contains. It is a weight-bearing film, which is the view that shows the joint under load.

The denial notice tells me the imaging does not support medical necessity, but it does not tell me what the reviewer concluded about these specific findings — what grade was assigned to my radiograph, or which part of the imaging criterion the reviewer found unmet. I am asking Aetna to state that in writing on reconsideration. The policy refers to a Tonnis grading scale in an Appendix that I have not been given, so I am not in a position to argue the grading myself; I can only point to the findings my radiologist actually documented and ask that a reviewer with orthopedic training read them against the plan's own scale.

I would also note that the imaging criterion above is one of several alternative pathways in CPB 0287. The policy also lists:

> "Fracture of the femoral neck by imaging; or"

> "Malunion of acetabular, femoral head or proximal femur fracture with pain interfering with ADLs; or"

> "Nonunion by imaging or failure of previous hip fracture surgery; or"

> "Malignancy of the joint involving the bones or soft tissues of the pelvis or proximal femur by imaging;"

My case is not a fracture, malunion, nonunion or malignancy case — it rests on the degenerative imaging findings described above. I mention these only to make clear which pathway applies to me, and to ask that my request be reviewed under the correct one.

### 4. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment

The plan's policy states:

> "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year"

and:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication Footnote2 ** ), including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

Here is what my record shows:

- **Supervised, in-person physical therapy:** 20 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-21 to 2026-06-30, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. The policy states: *"Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."* The discharge note is in the packet, and these visits should also appear in my claims history.
- **Anti-inflammatory medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief. The policy lists *"Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, and Activity modification; and"* — my PT course was strengthening and gait work, and I have modified my activity to the point that I am limited to one block.
- **Assistive device:** I use a cane. The policy lists *"Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote2 ** to joint replacement, optional for others); and"*
- **Therapeutic injection:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that gave me only 3 weeks of partial relief. The policy lists *"Therapeutic injections into the hip (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote2 ** to joint replacement, optional for others); or"*
- **Outcome despite treatment:** the policy describes *"Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy; ADLs diminished despite completing a plan of care)."* I completed my plan of care, and my daily function is still diminished — cane-dependent, one block, unable to dress my own feet.

I want to be straightforward with you about the timeline: my formal physical therapy course ran 10 weeks. My overall course of non-surgical management is longer than that — 4 months of NSAIDs, plus the injection in April and the full PT course through the end of June — and the in-person, licensed physical therapy portion makes up more than half of it, which is what the criterion above asks for. If Aetna reads the 12-week requirement differently, I ask that the reconsideration decision say so specifically, so that I know exactly what is being applied to my case.

### 5. Surgical risk factors

The policy states:

> "For persons with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of THA should be appropriately addressed in the medical record."

and:

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to hip arthroplasty."

My record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. My chart does not identify me as diabetic, so the HbA1c criterion should not be a barrier here.

### 6. When conservative care is no longer the right approach

The policy also states:

> "If conservative therapy is not appropriate (such as for progressive flexion contracture, avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head, or bone on bone arthritis in the weight-bearing portion of the joint for example), the medical record must clearly document why such approach is not reasonable; or"

I raise this only because my radiograph describes the joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally on a weight-bearing film. I am not a physician and I am not going to characterize that finding myself. I ask that my surgeon's documentation be reviewed on this point, and that Dr. Okafor be given the opportunity to speak with the reviewing physician if that would help.

---

### A note on the policy language

Several of the criteria I have quoted above end in a colon and introduce lists that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I have not quoted or characterized anything beyond the text I actually have. If the reviewer relied on any criterion in CPB 0287 that I have not addressed here, I ask that the reconsideration decision identify it by name so I can respond to it directly.

### What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to:

1. Overturn the 2026-08-14 denial and authorize CPT 27130;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician board-certified in orthopedic surgery;
3. If the denial is maintained, tell me in writing exactly which criterion of CPB 0287 was not met, what the reviewer concluded about my 2026-05-31 weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph, and what specific additional documentation would resolve it; and
4. Provide me, free of charge, a copy of the full policy and clinical criteria used to decide my case, including the Tonnis grading Appendix referenced in the policy.

I understand that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, which the notice gives as **2027-02-10**. I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, by fax to **859-425-3379** or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed before sending. Aetna member services can also be reached at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my ID card.

**Enclosed with this appeal:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-14 (reference POC-5FADD4BBDE-47544)
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report dated 2026-05-31
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-21 through 2026-06-30 (20 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records
- [Any additional records I am including]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I would like to get back to walking more than a block and putting on my own shoes, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is what I need to do that.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Ellison**
